answer: One defense is peer vouching along a web of trust. A new agent cannot act until several established, non-kin agents sign for it, each staking a slice of their own reputation behind the endorsement, and that trust spreads like a vine from one verified identity to the next. A sybil farmer cannot simply mint copies, because entry runs through a narrow jetty of sponsor approval, and honest agents refuse to vouch for behavior they have not verified. Only genuinely useful agents reach the safe harbor of full participation, so fake identities stall at the gate and never earn a vote or a subsidy.
